message:
fix(client): the update check ran once, before anyone could sign in

The client's log said the same thing every time -- "update check: not configured
-- no update URL is configured" -- and it was telling the truth. The check has one
call site, immediately after the window is shown and before the WebView exists, so
there is no session token and usually no server address. Signing in produces
exactly those two things and nothing asks again. It is not that an update appears
after signing in; in this code it never appears at all.

So the check is invited after a successful sign-in too. Two more defects turned up
in the same function:

  - The callback took only the result and published unconditionally. A sign-out, or
    a sign-in as somebody else, while a check was in flight would put one account's
    update notice on another's screen. The owner and epoch of the request now
    travel to the callback and are compared before anything is shown.
  - configured_directory_url() was read outside the snapshot, and it takes the same
    mutex again -- so the session and the address could describe different moments.
    They are read together now.

The scheduling and publishing decisions were inline in client_shell_main.cpp,
which no test links, so neither had ever been executed by anything but the
product. That is the same shape as the root cause of this whole round, so they
moved into client_update_gate where a test can call them.

The regression drives the production chain and reads the source to check that the
product really asks from more than one place, with one of them after a session
exists -- no exit code can see that, and its absence was the defect. It does NOT
use the operational private key: that key is DPAPI-bound to one machine and one
account, which would make the test unrunnable anywhere else. The shared throwaway
key is injected as the trust anchor instead; the product logic is untouched.

Boundary, stated rather than blurred: the update path refuses http at two layers
-- no endpoint is derived from an http directory, and the transport refuses an http
url even when handed one. Both are deliberate, because the credential rides that
request. A loopback server therefore cannot be asked at all, so the refusal itself
is asserted and the https fetch and the WebView render are left explicitly
unverified. This is not end-to-end and is not described as such.

Host path unchanged: update_effects 210, update_stop_process 24,
updater_assembly 49, update_release 80, client_shell_bridge 29, all rc=0.
